critical_code_review_comments: server.py::admin_book_diagnose (line 2010) — the endpoint accepts `probe_bytes` as a bool query param and probes ALL images on ALL pages when page_no is not set. On a 300-page book with 300 images this is 300 sequential storage.get_object calls in a request handler; response time is bounded only by the network. Consider (a) capping the probe count when page_no is None, or (b) parallelising with asyncio.gather + a semaphore. Not blocking for the immediate operator-diagnostic use case, but worth a note.

server.py::admin_book_diagnose — the doc-comment mentions `width_px/height_px 0` as a failure signal, but the response only includes those via the embedded db.files record (file_record.width_px/height_px). Fine as-is, but if a future consumer expects a top-level width_px/height_px in the block report they'll be surprised. Doc-only nit.

server.py::admin_book_diagnose — file_record projection excludes `_id` (good) but includes `is_deleted`. The endpoint doesn't currently skip soft-deleted files, which is arguably the right choice for a diagnostic (you want to SEE them) but the caller has to filter. Consider surfacing this in the comment.
RecentExportsDialog.jsx — the auto-load pattern `if (open && data === null && !loading && !error) load()` still runs inside render (mentioned in prev iteration). Cleaner as useEffect. Not blocking.

rca of the issue: Bug 1 was a classic Python UnboundLocalError: `render_timings` was previously assigned only inside the `else` branch (non-cover-spread path), so cover_spread=true hit the shared `_emit_job_summary(...)` call with the name never bound in that frame, raising UnboundLocalError before the try/except could swallow it. Fix at server.py:943 hoists the `render_timings: dict = {}` initialisation above the `if cover_spread:` branch so both paths share a live binding. Bug 2 was a missing capability — a read-only per-page inspector was needed to point at production book 361de655 (which doesn't exist in preview) and pinpoint the page 21 WeasyPrint hang; the new admin_book_diagnose endpoint provides that with an optional bytes-probe (Pillow verify + decode) so the operator can distinguish orphan file_record vs zero-byte upload vs decode-hang scenarios without kicking off a real render. Bug 3 was symptom-vs-cause: iteration 18's `credentials:'include'` masked the real divergence — RecentExportsDialog was the ONE component still using raw fetch instead of the shared axios `api` client whose interceptor injects the Bearer header. Switching to `api.get('/admin/recent-exports')` eliminates the fork; verified live that the outbound request now carries `Authorization: Bearer …` from the interceptor and no cookie header from a stale credentials:'include'.
